reason: Landlords chose to let property and bring the claims. They should fund the courts that hear them.
Renters already have little. Extra cost or risk should not land on them while the courts catch up.
Taxpayers fund courts for everything else. A separate housing tribunal keeps eviction cases from clogging the rest.
I rent and I am old. I could not cope if costs or a rushed case fell on me.
Local desks sound sensible. Most disputes should be settled near home without a judge.
Landlords benefit from the system, so a fee on claims is fair, if it really goes to courts.
Housing cases need their own judges. Waiting years helps nobody, tenant or landlord.
A fee that pays for the courts is simple. People who use the service pay for it.
Landlords should not expect everyone else to pay for their disputes. Ring-fence the fee.
I rent from the council. Whatever happens, renters should not be the ones paying or losing their homes.
Settling things locally is quicker and kinder than court, as long as nobody is forced.
A proper tribunal with its own staff is worth the tax money. Courts do need fixing.
